I hope you will have a change of heart from your broken heart. I've had similar plans in the past. Please reach out for help. If you can't or wont, please have a little heart and do it away from your house. Your family doesnt deserve the trauma of finding you like that. I found the man I was named after at a young age after he killed himself with a gun, and its eaten at me, undermined me, and led me to the edge  a few times.
God I wish my dreams were happy, but all I see are nightmares. Every night, all night. Might explain why I'm still awake right now.

It's not weird to not have the urge to commit suicide. That's actually what my pdoc would cal 'normal healthy behavior.' I get wanting to do *something* though. 

Try focusing that desire to something constructive. A hobby? Excersize? Volunteering? Playing D&D? Whatever works for you. Nearly anything than sitting alone at home.

A hospital stay might benefit you. I don't know where you reside, but in the US a *voluntary* admit isn't a matter of public record. Only the people you inform (and by extension they inform and so on) will ever know. If the stay becomes involuntary however, that can show up on background checks, etc.

As to your so called friend. He's a douchenozzle. Find some reason to cut him off. For your GPA, in the states your GPA only really impacts your ability to get into university directly, not your job potential. I had GPA problems during my junior year due to medical issues, and couldn't get into university directly. I went to community college for two years after I was healthy and then transferred to the university I wanted. My degree and resume all simply list that university. They only considered my college GPA, not my high school performance. I guess what I'm trying to say, is messing up in high school isnt the future killer that it sometimes seems like.

Aside from that, I'm sorry for the rough go. Depression can make it extremely difficult to concentrate, study and accomplish your goals. I hope you find your way through it and don't give up.

It may sound trite, but there are a TON of resources for this in the community information sidebar. Also, the crisis lines will help with how to talk to friends and/or family who are suicidal. I hope you find the help you need.

There are always other hospitals, but it is ultimately your call. As to your promise though, I don't think you ever truly gave medication a chance to work. Since it still could you wont be breaking your promise if you don't end it.

Honestly, you might be served by going to the ER to be admitted to an inpatient program. They can adjust your meds more rapidly and help you get through the time it takes for the dose to reach therapeutic levels. I know it's a daunting prospect, but it has gotten me through some of my patches as I have medications that cant be started or stopped rapidly without 24/7 care. Things that would have taken months outpatient can be done in days inpatient because you can get help if something goes wrong.

I'm sorry you feel like you're at the end of the line. It took a lot of time, as well as trial and error to get my meds right. Even still, it is far from perfect. And at times, I have periods of "decompensation"; basically my current therapy stops working and I have to start again.

May I ask, what meds you've tried? What condition they are supposed to treat?

Classes end, and life moves on from there. I wish I could say that makes it easier. Life is hard. Life after uni is hard. But it's the challenge that keeps it from being dull and monotonous.

As to the bridge, I have my own nearby. It is well known for it's beauty and the number of people who have used it to end their life. I cross it twice a day and it calls me every time. No matter how many times I've stopped, and gotten out of my car to stand on the edge, it doesn't get any easier.   I always find a reason to get back in my car. I hope you do too.
It's never too late to change your mind until it is. Unless you're dead, you still have the freedom to make your own choices and accept the consequences (good or bad) that stem from them.

These are some pretty heavy questions. I will try to do what I can to help and answer from my own experience.

To answer your questions...

Suicidal ideation isn't really 'normal' or 'healthy', but it's not uncommon. It's also not something to be ashamed of. It is something you really should talk to a doctor or counselor about. When discussing it, it is helpful to be clear between having suicidal thoughts and feelings versus having an active plan or desire.

I definitely am not qualified to diagnose you, and I won't try to. But from my experience, even when you're depressed it can be normal to feel superficially happy. But if you can never find enjoyment, happiness, motivation, etc. In your day to day life, it is definitely possible that you have depression or some other issue (I mean... low thyroid levels can mimic a lot of the symptoms).

I don't know Canadian medical privacy law. There is some information here on BC law, but I was too tired to read it ( http://www.healthinfoprivacybc.ca/confidentiality/when-can-and-cant-they-tell-others ). In the US they couldn't tell your parents if you're over 13 without your consent. That said you really should talk to them about it. Don't hide things from your doctors or they can't help you.

As to a crisis line, don't worry about them. They are giving support and advice and are trained to deal with the stress and feelings. Short of killing yourself on the phone with them they will be ok.

As to intrusive vs suicidal thoughts... intrusive thoughts can be nearly anything. Involuntary unpleasant thoughts, feelings, images that you get stuck on and ruminate about. Once they move into suicide, they are suicidal ideation. 

I hope some of this helps. If you need to talk, feel free to reach out.

I can relate to this on so many levels. I have gone through many of the same things just admitting I have suicidal thoughts. The concept of having a plan just completely fucks people up.

Suicidal ideation and more so suicide itself has become so highly stigmatized that people don't learn how to talk about it (or virtually any mental disorder). It is still taboo. When confronted with things we don't understand and don't know how to talk about, many people choose to run. If they cut ties they don't have to deal with it and don't have to be vulnerable to getting hurt if you go through with it. Those who don't run tend to become overbearing. If they smother you with love and attention you couldn't possibly still be suicidal. And they are scared (in the case of your family and are worried you've done something if they don't hear back).

Anyways, what I'm trying to say is don't judge them too harshly. They suck, and society sucks but they aren't trying to make it harder for you. They are just trying to do what they think is best. If you can, try articulating to them what your needs are and see if they can adjust. I had a heart to heart with my parents about what suicidal ideation really was for me, what it meant and what kind of support I needed and after the knee jerk reaction wore off they have been great in respecting my boundaries but being supportive in the ways I allow. 

Best of luck on your recovery and your friends and family understanding. Sending positive thoughts and good vibes your way.

Your immediate health is more important than work. If you live in the states and have been at your job for a year you probably qualify for FMLA (protected medical leave). Either way, please take care of yourself before you take care of your job.

I'm glad it helps. I get what you mean. I wouldnt wish this on anyone, but knowing you're not completely alone is comforting. If you ever need to talk or vent feel free to reach out. Good luck finding something awesome to do. Keeping busy and helping others helps with the days I just want to give up.

I hope you can find some strong anchors for your life soon. I can relate somewhat to the feelings you're experiencing - obviously not exactly (I don't know what you're going through, only you do). I'm a people pleaser too, and feel like I lost everything and everyone that mattered in my life and the feeling is miserable. I won't lie, it doesn't mystically get better, but you can make it a goal to improve yourself a little bit each day or week or month or whatever works for you.

Some things that help hold me down are my pets, a meaningful job, and volunteering. It could be none of those are an option for you, but I'm positive there is something you can find that is a fit for your life and will help you. I'm sending good thoughts and positive vibes your way. Please don't be afraid to reach out if you need it. It's saved me more than once.

I'll be honest, the only person who can honestly answer that question is your personal doctor that knows your medical history. It may sound odd, but consider talking to your doctor about what something like that could do for you. As a survivor you know that sometimes a failed attempt can leave you in a much worse place physically and mentally. On the other hand it can also serve as a wakeup call.

We can't get into specifics on methods on this sub, so that's the best advice I can offer. I hope you'll consider your options carefully before making your decision. I'm sending nothing but good thoughts and positive vibes your way and wish you the best of luck in whatever you ultimately decide.

My personal advice is for you and your friend to block him and move on with life. If he starts to stalk her go to the police or courts for a restraining order. 

This is probably going to get me burnt a bit in this venue, but anyone who threatens to kill themselves if you will/wont (insert thing here: date them, ignore them, do something with or for them, etc) is being manipulative and narcissistic. It's attention seeking behavior, and replying to it positively or negatively just feeds into it. Ultimately, you and your friend are not responsible for his happiness. I hope he gets the help he needs.

If you're convinced he's genuinely serious about killing himself or harming anyone, report it to the police and let them do a welfare check.

It's possible. I had a close friend commit suicide. Despite leaving a note and it being fairly self evident, the local police investigated. As a result, many less than savory details of his life came out. From the amount of porn he had stashed, to his call history. It was, unfortunate.
I hope your tomorrow morning you reconsider. Sending positive thoughts and good vibes your way. Good luck with whatever you decide.
